during the current year. The position will be reviewed in the middle of the FY and demand for additional
allocation will be processed accordingly.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee fails to understand as to why 24619 sanctioned applications were kept pending
for disbursement despite availability of funds. These had to be carried over to the next financial
year, thereby cutting short the already reduced BE for 2017-18. The Committee recommends that
appropriate steps may be taken by the Ministry to contain the vicious circle of carrying over of the
pending applications to subsequent financial years. The Committee may be informed of the
achievements made in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
A target of establishing 75 new PMEGP units each with investment of 
` 8-10 lakh was set in each
district of the country. The Committee noted that only 200 districts out of 676 districts of the country could
achieve this target. (Para 163)
Action Taken
In order to have equal distribution of targets and to achieve inclusive growth, a target of minimum of
75 projects have been allocated to all the districts in each State with average MM per project been taken as
` 2.00 lakhs (project cost ` 8-10 lakh). During the FY 2015-16, only 208 districts out of the total 676
districts have achieved the target of 75 projects. Efforts were made to achieve the target of 75 units for each
district, State KVIC, Principal Secretaries of State Government were requested from time to time to monitor
the Scheme. District level advisory committees headed by the Hon'ble MPs of respective district also monitor
the Scheme. However, various other factors including availability of raw material, industrial infrastructure,
skilled manpower etc. also contributes to the establishment of micro units in the districts.

40
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee finds it difficult to convince itself of the logic adduced by the Ministry that
PMEGP units could not be set up as per the target due to shortage of raw materials, industrial
infrastructure and skilled manpower, which is contrary to the concept of PMEGP wherein Skill
Development is part of the Scheme based on local raw material. The Committee is therefore, of the
view that setting up of 75 units in each District should be made mandatory and Zonal and State
Heads of KVIC may be advised to comply with the condition.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee observes that all the States, barring Kerala, have missed the target of setting up 75
PMEGP projects per year per District, significantly. If even 75 Micro Enterprises of ` 10 lakh investment
could not be set up in not more than 200 districts in a year then there is a question mark on the effectiveness
of the scheme like PMEGP . The Committee wonders the efficacy of KVIC, DIC and KVIB institutions in
these States which are responsible for outreach and implementation of the Scheme. The Committee may be
informed about the steps, beyond the usual advisory, that have been taken in respect of these State agencies
for failing to meet even a meager target which was set by the KVIC after taking into account the available
funds, average cost of each PMEGP project and desirability for equal distribution of development. The
committee may be informed if the frequency of meetings held by the Review Committee under the Chairmanship
of local MP and what are the major observations. (Para 166)
Action Taken
With the advent of web based PMEGP, the details of movement of the application, meetings at the level
of DLTFC, uploading of data and movement of sanctions to banks and finally approval process of banks and
communication of sanction to the applicants could be monitored through the portal in a transparent manner.
Review meetings at the level of local MPs have been recommended and Ministry has urged all Hon'ble MPs
to chair such meeting to monitor the progress of PMEGP.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee takes note of the limitations encountered in implementing the Scheme, since
it is being implemented largely through State agencies which are outside the control of KVIC.
However, the Committee recommends that Zonal and State Heads of KVIC be made accountable for
not achieving the recommended target of 75 units in each District.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee recommends that the Ministry must do a survey of survivability of PMEGP projects
beyond 3 years till they repay the Bank loan. The Ministry must also conduct a Survey of the PMEGP units
that have graduated to Small or Medium units. (Para 169)
Action Taken
PMEGP is a back-ended subsidy scheme, MM subsidy is deposited in the Term Deposit Receipt (TDR)
account in the name of the beneficiary and is adjusted against the Bank loan after three years upon physical
verification of units. 100% physical verification of PMEGP units is compulsory, the verification is done
generally during the third year of the setting up of project. As per the physical verification reports, about

41
80% of the units are found working. No survey has yet been made on the survivability of PMEGP units
neither beyond three years nor to ascertain the PMEGP units that have graduated from Micro to Small/
Medium units.
A provision has also been made in the guidelines that the Nodal offices of concerned agencies viz.
KVIC/KVIB/DIC will visit the units atleast once in every 6 months after their setting-up in order to check
their status and provide necessary guidance/handholding and mentoring. A mandatory joint inspection by the
nodal officers of the implementing agency ( viz. KVIC, KVIB or DIC) and the Financing Bank Branch
officials may also be carried out in scheduled manner after one month, three months and every 6 months.
This would also aid in recovery of the loans and put check on projects becoming NPA.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee feels desirability of having timely a survey of survivability of projects under
PMEGP to keep a check on NPA. During its study visit, the Committee observed that there was a
variation in the figures on NPA under PMEGP provided by Banks, and KVIC, with Banks clearing
NPA under PMEGP to the extent of 70%. Therefore, it is essential to do a survey of survivability of
projects under PMEGP. The survey would also facilitate in ascertaining the number of units that
could graduate into Small or Medium units, thus further enabling the implementing agencies to
provide necessary hand-holding to those units that could not graduate into SMEs.
Recommendation/Observation
Having observed the structural complexities in PMEGP that have denied lull and timely utilization of
allocated Funds and keeping in view that average cost of a PMEGP project is between 
` 8-10 lakhs as per
Ministry's estimates, which can be covered under the MUDRA loan that is easy to access and with lower rate
of interest, the Committee agrees with Ministry's suggestion that all the projects upto ` 10 lakhs could be
covered by the MUDRA yojna. New and even old expansion projects beyond ` 10 lakh to ` 25 lakhs may be
covered under PMEGP. The Ministry may change the objective and structure of the Scheme accordingly.
(Para 172)
Action Taken
PMEGP is a credit-linked subsidy programme, aimed at generating self-employment opportunities
through establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. Margin Money subsidy of 15-35% is
admissible to the beneficiaries belonging to different categories. Micro units having a maximum project cost
of `25 lakh are covered under PMEGP. MUDRA is a different Scheme being implemented by Department of
Finance, which provide loans from `50 thousand to `10 lakh to existing as well as new units. PMEGP is
available for new units only. As most of the applications under PMEGP are for loan below `10 lakh, KVIC
was requested that the details of PMEGP applicants could also be shared with MUDRA so that the applicants
seeking loans upto `10 lakh may opt for Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY). However, as there is no
subsidy under MUDRA Scheme, the prospective entrepreneurs prefer PMEGP scheme and huge number of
applications are received under PMEGP, which restrain the move for changing the objective and structure of
the Scheme.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee understands that the Schemes of PMEGP and MUDRA are different in their
structure and operationability owing to the fact that the former is a Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme

42
while the latter is a loan Scheme. Further, while PMEGP is administered by Ministry of MSME,
MUDRA is under Department of Financial Services. The Committee takes note of the Ministry's
submission that prospective entrepreneurs prefer PMEGP Scheme due to its subsidy components.
However, it remains a fact that only 1/3 of the applicants got benefits under the Scheme while rest
are rejected for want of funds. Also, it was brought before the Committee that PMEGP loans below
10 lakhs, get reflected under MUDRA. However, there was a difference of opinion in this regard
between Department of Financial Services (SIDBI) and M/o MSME (KVIC).
In view thereof, the Committee is of the opinion that regardless of the Schemes/Programmes
under which assistance is offered, the ultimate aim of the Government should be to benefit the
maximum number of deserving entrepreneurs. Accordingly, the Committee desires that M/o MSME
may co-ordinate with Department of Financial Services and bring about a synergic solution regarding
the overlapping structures between PMEGP and MUDRA, resulting in a possible interoperability of
both the Schemes.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee may also be apprised if the MPDA claims particularly in respect of artisans, submitted
by the KIs are actually verified by (he KVIC and method of verification adopted. The Committee may be
informed whether there have been cases when Khadi artisans are given work only on monthly, i.e. for a few
months and remain idle for most part of the year. (Para 182)
Action Taken
The MMDA claims of Khadi Institutions (KIs) as well as Khadi artisans are paid by DBT portal specially
designed for this purpose. The MMDA incentives of artisans are directly paid into their Aadhaar seeded bank
account, and their incentives are automatically calculated with reference to their wages earned in the concerned
quarters.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that Aadhaar can only ensure that the Bank account actually
belongs to a particular person. The Committee however is interested to know the steps being taken
to ensure that incentives actually go to the genuine artisans.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes with concern very low enrolment under MPDA scheme in the NER. The expenditure
of MPDA earmarked for NER has been negligible every successive year. As per the definition of Khadi in
the Act, the mandate of KVIC is to encourage silk, cotton and/or woolen hand spun and hand woven cloths.
Considering that North Eastern region has rich spun and woven textile tradition, KVIC should not have any
reason for such low penetration of MPDA in that region. The Committee may be informed if the textile
tradition of NE complies with the definition of Khadi under the Act, and why KVIC has not been able to
propagate the MPDA and other Khadi schemes in NE and money under MPDA, KRDP , SFURTI and
ASPIRE remains unspent. In view of such indifferent performance, the KVIC must take a hard look of the
performance of its regional set up and KVIB in these States and inform the Committee of their lackluster
performance. KVIC must encourage and revive the textile tradition in NER through MPDA and S&T schemes.
(Para 188)

43
Action Taken
The MMDA is passed on to KIs based on their actual production during a quarter. The payment of
MMDA to North- East region is comparatively lesser than that of other region mainly due to absence of good
number of KIs in N.E. region.
In all schemes NER is given special treatment and efforts are on to register more KIs under the fold of
KVIC. KVIC is implementing Science and Technology scheme in North East region by allotting 10% of
funds out of its Annual Action Plan every year. Much more efforts will be made to encourage Research
Organizations to undertake R&D projects in NE region.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is concerned to note the poor performance of KVIC Schemes in NER which
has its own District textile and Craft traditions. The Committee recommends that KVIC must
support Districts spinning and weaving traditions in NER and upscale it.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee wonders if the objective of the Scheme is to reduce reliance on subsidy, how the Ministry

The MPDA scheme is one of the tranche conditions of KRDP to be implemented in the field in place of
the existing MDA to extend the benefit to Artisans and Karyakartas. The main object of the KRDP is to
extend benefit to Artisans and Karyakartas, besides providing for rationalization of subsidy by phasing out

linked pricing for khadi products. The quantum of allocation of subsidy under MPDA will not relate to
KRDP allocation. KRDP allocation to meant for to reform the Khadi activities so that KIs will become self-
sustainable.

conditions of the KRDP. It is also understood that the KIs can continue to benefit from both the
programmes, which means that KRDP does not intend to eliminate the subsidies currently being

the simultaneous operations of KRDP and MPDA clearly bringing out the difference in their objectives

Action Taken
Under the Scheme 'Support for Entrepreneurial and Managerial Development of SMEs through
Incubators', 440 innovative ideas were approved in the Twelfth Five Year Plan up to 31.3.2017. The main
objective of the scheme is to promote emerging technological and knowledge-based innovative ventures that

Enterprises (MSMEs). The scheme is implemented through duly approved Host institutes / Business Incubators
(HI/BI). The purpose of the small dose of assistance provided under the present scheme is to support
students / ex-students of science and technology and entrepreneurs to try out their innovative ideas (in
processes and products) at the laboratory or workshop stage and beyond (to the extent possible) -to carry
forward the idea from its mere conception to 'know-how' and then to 'do how' stage. It may thus be seen
that the scheme is designed for sustaining, at some basic or introductory level, the incubation of ideas that
would have otherwise been lost for want of support.
The guidelines do provide for situations where many Host Institutions, where other similar programmes
for enriching and incubating innovations are already on, this assistance could be dovetailed within them, by
way of an additional encouragement / sustenance, without leading to duplication or unnecessary double
benefits.
Monitoring is accomplished through reviewing progress reports from His, and release of subsequent
installment. It is for Host Institution or its BI to benchmark the expectations from its students and
entrepreneurs (and their ideas) at the level that is considered appropriate and to provide the level of assistance
that is actually required to operationalise ideas.
The financial sanction orders issued to the approved HI/BIs, whose proposed ideas/concepts have
been duly approved, will be officially informed that the expenditure incurred against sanctioned funds will be
open to inspection by the sanctioning authority, CAG, CCA in the MoMSME. Copies of the said sanction
orders are also sent to the Principal Director of Audit, Economic & Service Ministry, New Delhi. However
this office has no any formal method of auditing the HI/BI.

Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is constrained to note that during first three years of the current Plan the utilization has been
meager. The Schemes have been repeatedly reframed and thereby withholding the expenditure pending the
mid-course review. The Third Party Review of all the components of NMCP in the beginning of 12th Plan,
had commended the utility of these components and recommended their continuation. The Committee finds
that these Third Party review, though selected through bidding, were conducted by the NIESBUD, which was
an autonomous organization under the Ministry and Quality Council of India, wherein Government has
significant stakes. That is why the Committee has been steadfast in its recommendation that the NMCP
Scheme must be Performance Audited by the CAG. The Committee may be informed of the salient outcomes
of the Audit for which CAG has already been requested and Ministry's compliance thereon. (Para 113)

58
Action Taken
In response to the letter of DC (MSME) to CAG requesting to undertake performance audit of NMCP
schemes (vide this office letter dated 03.01.2017), CAG had sought following information from DC (MSME)
vide letter dated 13.02.2017:
a. Brief details of the six schemes including their background, objectives, activities, implementation
programme and target beneficiaries.
b. Budgeted estimates as well as the Actual Expenditure incurred on these six schemes since inception
to date, on year to year basis.
The above details sought by CAG from O/o DC (MSME) have been sent vide letter dated 06.03.2017.
It may be seen that this Ministry has complied with all requirements and further action vests with the CAG.
Recommendation/Observation
No information has been provided on the progress made in the utilization of $134 Million ADB assistance
for the remaining SFURTI scheme. The Committee may be informed of terms of this ADB assistance,
annual Budget support that will be required for availing this assistance and the schedule of implementing
the SFURTI scheme. (Para 151)
Action Taken
Asian Development Bank (ADB) assistance for SFURTI is being negotiated and is not yet finalized.
Only a technical appraisal by ADB has happened. The same would be pursued for faster approval and
finalization of MoU.
Recommendation/Observation
PMEGP is a flagship Scheme of the Ministry. Although Ministry has been receiving large number of
applications but it is able to include only 1/3 applications for benefits and has to reject remaining 2/3 rd
applications, for want of funds allocated. (Para 156)
Action Taken
During FY 2016-17, `l 100 cr. were allocated towards PMEGP Margin Money Subsidy at BE stage.
This was reduced to `l082.90 crores at RE stage. Whole of the allocation of ` l082.90 cr. has been released
to KVIC. By the end of the FY 2016-17 PMEGP has achieved Margin Money disbursement of ` 1280.93
crores assisting 52912 micro enterprises. About 20,000 projects already sanctioned by the Banks was
available on 31.03.2016, which would be disbursed during the current year 2017-18.
Recommendation/Observation
Expenditure of Rs 413 crore during 2016-17 is being incurred out of budget allocation of 
` 1000 crore
for financial year 2015-16 under PMEGP . During 2016-17 available money under PMEGP has been
` 1500 crore and the expenditure has been only ` 700 cr. till December 2016. The Committee wondered
whether it will be possible to incur remaining amount of ` 800 crore in last 3 months. The Committee also
sought to know whether some budget of this year will be utilized in the next year. (Para 159)

59
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee also observes that Rs 413 crores were carried over to 2016-17 from the previous year's
RE whose release was delayed. As such for year 2016-17 Rs 1513 crores [` 1100 crore (BE) + Rs 413 crores
(carried forward from previous FY)] were available. Of which by 31.12.16, Rs 875 crores were released by
the Ministry as Margin Money. That leaves Rs 640 crore unspent for last quarter of 2016-17. Even of the
released amount of Rs 875 crores, only about Rs 660 crores have actually been disbursed by the Banks.
Therefore almost half the allocation is not actually disbursed till very last quarter of current Financial Year.
The Committee has been repeatedly questioning the prudent financial management of the scheme and
complicated structure that delays prompt disbursal to beneficiary. In view of the above facts, the Committee
finds that the situation has not improved much. (Para 161)
Action Taken (on paras 159 & 161)
During FY 2016-17, `l 100 cr. were allocated towards PMEGP Margin Money Subsidy at BE stage.
This was reduced to ` l082.90 cr. at RE stage. An unspent balance of `343 cr. alongwith `70 cr. towards
interest earned and margin money refunded were already available with KVIC. Whole of the allocation of
`l082.90 cr has been released to KVIC during 2016-17. The PMEGP on-line e-portal developed by KVIC
was been put into operation w.e.f. 1st July, 2016. The system was new and initially taking lot of time by the
agencies to operate the same. In addition, during the FY 2016-17, beside the cases applied on the on-line
system, there were lot of old cases already sanctioned by the Banks off-line. All the nodal banks accounts
were closed w.e.f. 1.7.2016 and the margin money from the field offices was withdrawn and deposited
with head office after proper re-conciliation. The project already sanctioned was also to be disbursed and
for them a separate portal from the Corporation Bank was developed and the old cases were uploaded on
this portal for disbursement. Thus, during 2016-17, the disbursement was made through three separate
modes viz.(a) complete off-line through nodal banks, (b) projects sanctioned offline by banks and disbursed
online through corporation Banks on DBT mode and (c) projects sanctioned and disbursed on PMEGP
e-portal. By the end of the FY 2016-17 PMEGP has achieved Margin Money disbursement of ` 1280.93
crore assisting 52912 micro enterprises. About 20,000 projects already sanctioned by the Banks are available
on 31.03.2016, which would be disbursed during the current year 2017-18. During the current year
2017-18, the on-line system has now been stabilized and the process will be faster.
Recommendations/Observation
The Committee had asked for the Performance Audit of the PMEGP for the 12th Plan period, which
was accepted by the Ministry. The Committee may be informed of the outcome and the compliance of the
Ministry. (Para 173)
Action Taken
Performance audit of PMEGP scheme by CAG team has already commenced. During 2016-17 the
records of KVIC-HQ- PMEGP Directorate, Mumbai were scrutinized and the field office of KVIC viz. State
Office Maharashtra (SOM) and State of Karnataka were selected for detailed inspection. The audit covered
the Scheme since inception in 2008 to March 2016.
Recommendation/Observation
If wages are to be determined on piece rate basis, then steps must be taken to improve productivity of
artisans without drudgery. KVIC must ensure production and supply of solar charkhas at reasonable rate

60
and any other improved version that enhances productivity, for which the Khadi and VI Grant for S&T may
be increased provided its utilization too is improved. (Para 180)
Action Taken
Welfare of Khadi artisans is primary objective of KVIC and all the policies of KVIC revolved around
improving their welfare and reduction of their drudgery. KVIC has periodically under taken various S&T
projects aiming at increasing their wages, production and productivity. Further KVIC has launched Solar
Charkha on trial basis and based on the outcome it will be taken on large scale.
Ministry of MSME and KVIC has emphasized for development and implementation of Solar Charkha in
the field to get more productivity as well as higher wages to the artisans. Keeping in view the importance
KVIC is taking all possible steps to extend the financial support for new Research and Development proposals
under development of solar power operated charkhas in different spindles.
However, the Khadi Gramodyog Sansthan, Ahmedabad vide their report has informed that the production
of hanks has been increased to 2.5 to 3 folds on the newly developed 12 spindle high speed amber charkha
running with solar energy i.e. 80 to 100 hanks from average of 35 hanks. Further, it has reported that the
wages has increased to four fold from an average earning of ` 100/- to ` 400/-.
KVIC has sanctioned following 5 R&D projects under solar charkha to strengthen the KVI sector in
terms of productivity as well as higher earnings to the artisans:
i. Design and development of 12 spindle high speed amber charkha running with solar energy
ii. Design and development of 08 spindle high speed amber charkha suitable for manufacturing
coarse yarn spun from very short staple length of Desi fibres.
iii. Field Trials/dissemination of 10 spindle solar charkha and solar looms technology
iv. Energy audit for solar charkhas Field trials of 16 spindle solar power driven charkha.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee also recommends that Khadi artisans may be covered under MNREGA for the purposes
of wages. The Ministry may expeditiously take up the issue with Ministry of Rural Development in this
regard to finalise the modalities. The Ministry may also inform the Committee about the outcome of discussions.
(Para 181)
Action Taken
Ministry of MSME has already taken up the matter with Ministry of Rural Development. (MoRD) to
provide coverage to khadi artisans under MGNREGA. Reply is awaited from MoRD.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee may be informed if all the khadi manufacturers are required to be registered with KVIC
under the KVIC Act. If not, are they still required to obtain Khadi mark which is given only by the KVIC,
and whether it may lead to certain conflict situations? (Para 186)
Action Taken
Khadi Mark Regulation 2013 came into existence on 19th July 2013 which applies to persons who are
engaged in the production, sale or trading of Khadi and Khadi products or who are desirous of producing,

61
selling or trading in Khadi and Khadi products and to certified Khadi Institutions (KIs) who hold a valid
Khadi Certificate issued by KVIC under clause (k) of sub-section(2) of Khadi and Village Industries Act
1956, read with Sub-Regulation (2) of Regulation 24 of Khadi and Village Industries Regulations, 2007.
Hence, it is mandatory for every person to obtain Khadi Mark Certificate who is engaged or desirous of
producing, selling or trading in Khadi and Khadi Products.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that the KIs which have attained A+ and A categories or those who have
been receiving MPDA assistance for more than five years, should be allowed to attain autonomy under
KRDP instead of continuing with MPDA. Instead, the KVIC should use MPDA money in assisting new or
weaker KIs. (Para 205)
Action Taken
As per the MMDA policy and tranche condition of KRDP scheme, MMDA has to be phased out and the
process of phasing out is under formulation stage.
All KIs which are categorized as "A", "A+" and "B" are eligible to avail financial support under KRDP
scheme. The KIs, who have availed KRDP scheme, are also eligible to continue to avail the benefit of the
MPDA subsidy.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee will be inclined to recommend that Ministry of Commerce should provide adequate
funds to KVIC for Export Promotion provided the KVIC is able to raise its activities and mobilize exportable
KVI commodities directly from the KVI institutions. The Ministry may accordingly take up the matter with
Ministry of Commerce. KVIC too should expediently fulfil necessary conditions to restore the Export Promotion
Council status. The KVIC must update the Committee in this regard. (Para 211)
Action Taken
KVIC is making all out efforts to restore the Export Promotion Council Status accorded to KVIC by
the Ministry of Commerce which will enable KVIC to avail the benefits of Market Access Initiative (MAI)
which are provided to deemed EPCs.
There are 1064 Nos. of KVI/REGP/PMEGP exporters enrolled with KVIC Export Promotion Council.
Maximum exports of KVI products are done through the merchant exporters since KVIC has been working
as a facilitator organization for exports. There is a provision of providing incentive in the form of 5% Freight
on Board (FOB) value of direct export of khadi products. Besides, KVIC has also been focusing on quality
participation in International Exhibitions and Buyer-Seller Meets abroad to tap new/emerging markets for
Khadi & VI products.
Recommendation/Observation
Taking note that the Ministry did not furnish any reply, the Committee wonders if it had any account of
the efficacy of its own scheme for the revival of stressed MSMEs. The Committee desires that the Ministry
may provide the number of such MSMEs rehabilitated/revived under the Framework and the cost incurred
by Banks in terms of restructuring the debts of such MSMEs. (Para 233)

62

As per information compiled by RBI, between reporting period 1.7.2016 to 31.12.2016, the number of
stressed loan cases, under the 'Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation of Micro, Small and Medium
Enterprises' referred to by various banks to the Committees set-up by them was to the tune of 41,417, out
of these 29595 cases have been resolved by the Committees.

Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is inclined to advise Ministry that industry associations too should be involved in the
Review Committee to assess the implementation of Public Procurement Policy. The Committee also recommends
that the Ministry should remind the administrative Ministries regarding policy directive to set up Grievance
Redressal Committee under a Joint Secretary as required under the Policy. (Para 243)
Action Taken
The composition of the Review Committee has been approved by the Cabinet while approving the
Policy. However, as per directions of Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee, meeting with
industry association has been conducted under the Chairmanship of Secretary, MSME. Further the grievances
received through Industry/Association are solved as and when received. As per the directions of the Review
Committee, procuring, Agency has already been requested to appoint a Nodal Officer who is looking the
implementation of PP Policy.
The Grievance Cell has been constituted in the O/o AS&DC, MSME as per the para 13 of the PP Policy
which clearly points out that a Grievance Cell is to be set up in the Ministry of MSME and that Cell will take
up the issues raised by the MSE with the concerned procuring agencies. Ministry of MSME has already
requested the procuring agencies for nominating Nodal Officer responsible for implementation of the PP
Policy in their organization.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee desires that the details of Prabhat Kumar Committee and its financial and legislative
implications may be informed to the Committee. The Committee may also be apprised if the Ministry has set

63
milestones for rolling out the Policy provisions in short and medium terms and benchmarks to assess the
success of Policy. (Para 260)
Action Taken
The Ministry of MSME, in December 2015, constituted Prabhat Kumar Committee to make
recommendations towards a national policy for MSMEs. The Committee has submitted its report to the
Ministry in January 2017 which is under examination. The Report is available on official website dcmsme.gov.in/
under this link http://dcmsme.gov.in/LegalFramework.htm
Recommendation/Observation
The MSME sector which is critical for the equitable growth and employment and entrepreneurship in
the economy, is a fact that can hardly be overstated. Though the Budget allocation for the Ministry of
MSME is not proportionate to the importance of this Sector, the Committee reiterates that the available
resources need to be used efficiently for the targeted objectives. The Committee has often noted the excuse of
Schemes being demand-driven for the under-utilization of allocations. If the Ministry is not convinced of
demand, then it should not seek allocation. The Ministry has not been able to generate demand for its
Schemes in a Sector which is wide spread over several sectors and is starved of any worthwhile policy
intervention. With number of KIs reducing and low employability of training courses the Committee wonders
the quality of monitoring at Ministry's level and efficacy of its institutional network in States and at grass
root levels. (Para 268)
Action Taken
The increase in Khadi Institutions (KIs) has registered a numerical increase but not in geometrical
ratio. However, KVIC has taken a policy initiative to bring is more KIs by opening the door for individuals,
partnership firms and companies and they can submit their application online and the process of registration
of certificate has been simplified, time-bound and online process.
KVIC through its Departmental and Non-Departmental Training centres conduct awareness programmes
throughout the country to propagate various schemes courses. Also the e-learning module have been uploaded
on web portal of KVIC in order to facilitate reach the un-employed youths. A call centre have been set up in
order to take a stock of candidates trained in Khadi and V.I. Sector and also to provide necessary guidance
about the schemes of KVIC to the beneficiary.
Recommendation/Observation
In view of CAG's repeated adverse observation of Ministry of MSME, the Committee has been asking
for Performance Audit of major Schemes by CAG and not the third party evaluation. The Committee may be
apprised of the outcome of the CAG's audit and its compliance. The Committee also recommends that Audit
Paras must be appropriately included in the Annual Report of the Ministry. (Para 274)
Action Taken
Ministry has taken up the issue of Performance Audit of all schemes. A request has been made vide
letter No. 3(1)/2016-EDI dated 16.12.2016 to CAG to undertake performance audit of the ATI Scheme as
per the recommendation of the Committee. Reply from CAG Headquarter is awaited.

64
O/o DC (MSME) has written a letter dated 09.05.2016 to CAG requesting them to conduct the
Performance Audit of 18 Tool Rooms & Technology Development Centres, under Audit Regulations 2007
(Chapter 7) of CAG Act, 1971. A team of Officers from CAG Office, New Delhi has visited this office in
Sep. 2016 and asked to provide various documents pertaining to Tool Rooms. All the documents have been
provided to them. Response from CAG is awaited. Further, O/o DC (MSME) has also written a letter dated
15.02.2017 to CAG requesting them to conduct Performance Audit of other major schemes of this Office.
Performance audit/evaluation study of PMEGP scheme has already been undertaken in the current
financial year. In the Annual Report of the Ministry for the year 2016-17, Audit Para No. 12.1 of Report No.
11 of 2016 has been shown under pending C&AG Audit Paras. However, the reply of this Audit Paragraph
has been uploaded on the Audit Para Monitoring System (APMS) web portal.

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises (Department of Heavy Industry) on the recommendations contained in the
Committee's Two Hundred and Eighty-first Report on the Demands for Grants (2017-18) pertaining to
Department of Heavy Industry.
2. Action Taken Notes received from the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises (Department
of Heavy Industry) in respect of the recommendations contained in the 281st Report have been categorized
as follows:
Chapter-I The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
The Committee notes that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as mentioned
in the Chapter - I of the Report.
Chapter-II The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
further in view of the Government's replies.
In respect of these recommendations, the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue them
further for the present.

Likewise, having taken note that the list of operative CPSEs under the Department is lesser by 7

support to its CPSEs to improve their performance' also requires considerable thought process and timely

operative CPSEs are retained and that their numbers are not further depleted. (Para 9)
Action Taken
The Department of Heavy Industry (DHI) has been undertaking performance appraisal of the CPSEs
regularly with a view to assess their inherent strength and potential to keep themselves afloat in the
current and emerging global economic environment of business. As a part of this exercise, while profit
making CPSEs are supported for further strengthening, the loss making CPSEs having the potential of

Further Recommendation
The Committee notes that the reply of the Department to its recommendation is in
contradiction to the stand submitted by DHI before the Committee with regard to the strategic
disinvestment of Bridge and Roof (B&R) Company Ltd. The Company was decided to be strategically
disinvested despite the fact that it was a century old CPSE that was making profit.
The Committee desires to know whether all profit making CPSEs would be supported for
further strengthening, based on performance or the decision for further strengthening would
depend upon the area of operation of a particular profit making CPSE.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee, however, considering the extensions of time and the cost overruns witnessed in case
of NATRIP, feels the need for a performance audit of the project to bring to light the exact reasons for
the aforesaid problems. This would bring more transparency in the execution of the Project and throw
light on the possible refinements needed in the managerial aspects and also act as guidance for future.
In this connection, it has been submitted to the Committee that the Department has constituted Committee
for the same. With respect to a performance audit by Controller and Auditor General (CAG), it was
appraised that the Department has a limited role. In this connection, the Committee draws attention to
the fact that the 'Performance Auditing Guidelines, 2014' of the CAG recognizes the report of a
Department- Related Standing Committee (DRPSC) as one of a source document for planning a performance
13

14
audit. Accordingly, the Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation to carry out a performance audit
of NATRIP . (Para 34)
Action Taken
DHI has no objection to the conduct of Performance Audit of NATRIP by CAG.
Further Recommendation
The Committee notes the reply of the Government. However, the Committee would like to
remind the Department that the Committee had recommended a performance audit to be carried
out. Accordingly, the Committee strongly reiterates its recommendation that all the requisite
process for a performance audit of NATRiP may be set in motion without any further delay. It
is for the Department to take action in this direction and report back to the Committee in this
regard.
Recommendation/Observation
On the issue of strategic disinvestments/closures, the Committee is of the considered view that
though the modern theories of government and economics want the Government to withdraw from
business, while deciding upon disinvestments/ closures, it is always prudent to keep in mind that CPSEs
are also meant to serve certain larger social causes. The Committee would like to make a mention of
an example in this regard i.e. the case of the decision for 100% disinvestment of HNL, a company that
was classified only as 'Incipient sick' in 2016. The Committee finds that the decision was taken despite
the dissent of DHI and the perception that the Company could have turned around with a modernisation
mill development plan that was under submission. The State Government is also understood to have been
responsive to the requests of FTNL with facilitative decisions. Taking this case as a cue, the Committee
recommends that the NITI Aayog shall be asked to take a more holistic view in case of decisions
regarding CPSEs that may be perceived to have a chance of progressing well with a little help. This is
based on the considered opinion of the Committee that CPSEs are still relevant and they may be allowed
reasonable and financially prudent chances to revive and restructure. (Para 65)
Action Taken
Hindustan Newsprint Limited has been recommended for strategic disinvestment and the process
is in progress. The quotations for 'Legal advisor' and 'Asset Valuer' have been received and are being
processed and the lender has been released for appointment of 'Transaction advisor'.
HNL has been in loss for the last four years from the year 2012-2013 due to the import pricing
of Newsprint. However the Company has been striving by making Writing and Printing Paper also, along
with Newsprint and selling of Pulp to TNPL etc. The Government of Kerala has been supporting the
Company by providing raw materials at a subsidized rate from its Forests. They have also allotted land
of 2670 Ha on lease basis for Captive Plantation. Water is also provided by the State Government for
manufacturing of Pulp and Paper.
Even though HNL is recommended for disinvestment, if GoI/DHI decides to revive, the Company
can make profits during this financial year subject to financial support of around `30 cr. As Working
Capital either from GoI or arranging through Banks Company can make Writing & Printing Paper and

15
Newsprint to meet the demand for Writing & Printing Paper as well as to retain the customers for
Newsprint.
Further Recommendation
The reply of the Department indicates the ambiguity in Governments approach with regard
to the disinvestment of HNL. Further, the reply also buttresses the concern expressed by the
Committee that HNL was decided to be disinvested despite its potential to turn around, may be
with a little more help in arranging working capital. Accordingly, the Committee again strongly
recommends that DHI, by its own opinion, may seek the feasibility of reversing the decision for
strategic disinvestment of HNL by taking into consideration, the fact that HNL has the potential
to revive into a profit making CPSE, with a little more hand holding from the Government.
Recommendation/Observation
Further, the Committee takes note of the submission of BHEL that the reduction in weighted
deduction from 200% to 150% in Income Tax for investment in R&D has affected the prospects of the
Company. Being the highest spender in R&D, as claimed by the management, BHEL stands to lose the
most because of this move. The fact that BHEL is the highest investor after the GoI in the Advance Ultra
Supercritical Project with an amount of 
` 270.00 cr. gives credibility to their said claim. Considering
this, the Committee recommends that the Government should think of restoring the IT deduction for R&D
investment to 200%. Further, the Committee views the Advance Ultra Supercritical Project as an avenue
which can help BHEL make up lost ground, if commercialized successfully. It is expected that the
Company will be executing their part in the project successfully. (Para 76)
Action Taken Replies
R&D represents a journey from mind to market. Further, progressive technological changes require
carrying out R&D activities on a continuous basis so as to provide belter or more efficient products,
services and solutions. In India, getting advanced technologies nowadays from outside is generally an
expensive and time-consuming affair, besides it does not inculcate self-reliance. It is therefore crucial to
incentivise companies and organisations taking risks by investing in R&D, which can lead to development
of indigenous technology and new products for benefiting the society. In this regard, Section 35 (2AB)
of Income Tax Act, 1961 provided for weighted deduction of 200% of the expenditure incurred by a
Company on scientific research on an approved in-house research and development facility from financial
year 2010-11 to 2016-17. This also facilitated promotion of R&D efforts in the Country, and has also
been an inducement for investing in in-house R&D activities by many companies/organisations. However,
the Finance Act 2016 amended the aforesaid section and reduced the weighted deduction from 200% to
150% from financial year 2017-18 to 2019-20, and also further restricted this to 100% from 01.04.2020.
The reduction in weighted deduction affects the income tax liability of many companies engaged in R&D
and innovation, including BHEL which is among the highest R&D spenders in the Country in the
engineering and manufacturing segment. Given the importance of R&D for any economy, it is important
for the Government of India to expand incentives so as to encourage companies and organisations to
carry out or expand R&D activity and also contributing to innovation in the Country. Hence, the
allowability of weighted deduction under section 35(2AB) of Income Tax Act should be restored to 200%
by the Govt. of India, as was available earlier. This will also facilitate companies and organisations in
contributing to the ecosystem of "Make in India" programme.

16
As regards the Committee looking forward to BHEL successfully executing its part in the "R&D
Project for development of Advanced Ultra Super-Critical (AUSC) Technology for Thermal Power
Plants", the Company has taken up the associated work on a mission mode and also initiated steps for
its implementation process. Further, all efforts are being and will be made for timely completion of the
R&D phase of the project within the envisaged schedule
Further Recommendation
The Committee notes that the reply of the Department is in tune with its recommendation
for restoration of the weighted deduction back to 200% in Income Tax for making investment
in R&D. It also notes that the "R&D Project for Development of Advanced Ultra Super-Critical
(AUSC) Technology for Thermal Power Plants" is being taken up in mission mode by BHEL and
measures are being adopted to complete it without time/cost overruns.
However, the Committee does not find in the reply any submission about the steps taken
by DHI for taking up the matter of restoration of the weighted deduction in Income Tax,
appropriately. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the matter may he taken up at
appropriate level and action taken in this regard may be furnished to the Committee. The
Committee also wants the Department to explore the possibility of providing special impetus to
R&D spending on the lines of priority accorded to CAPEX.

17
CHAPTER-IV
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE
DESIRE FURTHER COMMENTS OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/observation
However, the Committee finds that out of ` 60.00 Cr. RE for 2016-17, the amount released till the
third week of February, 2017 is only ` 24.0184 Cr. During the remaining period of little more than a
month, ` 29.4963 Cr. is expected to be released. The Committee would have been impressed had the funds
for the Scheme been utilized in a more spread out fashion. Even so, it is expected that the remaining
funds would be utilized during the year as anticipated by the Department. (Para 55)
Action Taken
During the financial year 2016-17 out of the allocated budget of ` 60.00 crore (R.E. 2016-17) an
amount of ` 59.75.00 crore was utilized and Grant-in-Aid was released to eleven project implementing
organizations whose proposals had been approved earlier under different components of the CG Scheme.
Recommendation/Observation
Regarding the Modernization of HEC, the Committee would like to bring to record its persistent
recommendations for the same as contained in its reports on DFG 2013-14, 2015-16 and 2016-17 of
DHI. The Committee cannot but register its disappointment on the lethargy shown by the Government
in addressing this matter for such a protracted time period. Having said this, the Committee now finds
it encouraging that HEC might be seeing light at the end of the tunnel with the signing of MoU with
the Russian company CNITMASH for setting up niche training centres for specialized training and all-
important Saraswat Committee report strongly favouring the Modernization of HEC. The Committee also
lends its whole-hearted support to the same and strongly objects to the transfer of HEC to the State
Government of Jharkhand, which might sound the death knell of a company of potential strategic
importance. A State Government cannot be expected to take over successfully into its folds a Company
of the nature and depth of HEC. It is recommended that the said move of the transfer of the Company
should be summarily dropped and expeditious approval of the recommendation of the Saraswat Committee
for the immediate funding of the requirements of HEC be undertaken, without any further delay. Further,
keeping in mind the possible of the forays of the Company into Defence related and other strategic areas
of manufacturing, the Committee also favours transfer of HEC as a Defence PSU under the Ministry
of Defence. (Para 83)
Action Taken
In order to revitalize HEC Ltd., a Revival cum Modernization Plan was prepared by M/s MECON,
envisaging a comprehensive overhaul of HEC's plants and facilities at an estimated cost of ` 956.48
crore.
Pursuant to discussion in PMO on modernization-cum-revival of HEC, an Expert Committee under
chairmanship of Dr. Sarswat, Member NITI Aayog was constituted to review the modernization plan of
17

18
HEC prepared by the Consultant (M/s. MECON) taking into account the business plan required for future
sustainability.
The expert committee carried out a thorough study of the modernization proposal. The Committee
reviewed the performance of the Company since its inception, analysed its core competence and visited
the plant to evaluate the present state of plant and machinery. The Committee held varied interactions,
not only with different levels of officials of HEC but also with the important stake holders in HEC's
products viz. Coal India Ltd. SAIL, Indian Railways, NPCIL, Defence organizations etc.
The Saraswat Committee had submitted its report in Jan, 2017. The Committee has strongly
recommended the revival of the HEC and observed that a manufacturing infrastructure like that of HEC
is very much necessary for country's aspiration to be self-aspiration in crucial strategic products.
The projected requirement of funds for the modernization and making the company liability free is
` 2252 cr. which includes a capital investment of ` 1252 cr. discharging of liability of ` 700 cr. and
requirement of working capital of ` 300 cr.
The recommendations of the Saraswat Committee are under consideration of the Department. As
a part of first phase of implementation of the recommendation of the Saraswat Committee, Cabinet in
its meeting dated 31.3.2017 has approved the proposal for monetization of land of 675.43 acres not
currently in use by HEC to the State Government of Jharkahnd to raise ` 742.98 crore and utilizing the
proceeds, inter-alia, for liquidation of statutory dues and other liabilities.
As regards the recommendation of the DRPSC for not transferring HEC to state Govt, of Jharkhand
and also being in favour of transfer of HEC as Defence PSU under the Ministry of Defence, the
recommendations of Committee have been noted by the Department. Appropriate action on these points
will be taken by the Government of India in consultation with all the stake holders.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee also feels that in keeping with the recommendations of the Saraswat Committee, the
Department should strongly consider selling out a part of HEC's surplus land at 
` 1.65 crore per acre
so that the HEC is enable to pay of all its liabilities and embark on a journey of success. (Para 84)
Action Taken
The Expert Committee recommended modernization of facilities with simultaneous discharge of
liabilities for long term sustainability of the Company . It also recommended provision of sufficient
working capital especially during construction/modernization period and source of fund identified
recommended by the Committee has been (i) disposal of land in two phases (a) for generating `743 cr.
by transferring 675 acres of land to Govt. of Jharkhand @ `1.10 cr. per acre and (b) generation of
around ` 1000 cr. by transferring additional land to Govt. of Jharkhand @ `1.65 cr. per acre, (ii) Loan
from Financial Institution, to be kept at minimum level for minimum interest burden, and (iii) support
from Govt. of India.
Cabinet in its meeting dated 31.3.2017 has approved the proposal for monetization of land of 675.43
acres not currently in use by HEC to the State Government of Jharkhand to raise ` 742.98 crore and
utilizing the proceeds, inter-alia, for liquidation of statutory dues and other liabilities.

19
As already stated the recommendation of the Saraswat Committee is under consideration of the
Department.
Recommendation/observation
The Committee note that HPC has run into losses from 2009-10 onwards owing to reasons like the
supply of raw materials getting affected due to gregarious flowering of bamboo, a concurrent ban on
supply of bamboo by the Government of Mizoram and the non- availability of coal from Meghalaya due
to the ban on the same by NGT. It is understood that the raw material availability for Nagaon & Cachar
Paper Mill has almost become normal and coal availability is expected to be resolved by March, 2017,
in view of broad gauge railway lines being made available by then. Further, a revival plan to the tune
of 
` 1,313 crore has been submitted, recently, to the Government under which ` 95 crore has been
provided during 2017-18 for the installation of Oxygen De-lignifications of plant and modern Boilers
at NPM and CPM. Considering the unique importance of the units of HPC in the NER emanating from
the fact that they are the main source of livelihood of a large section of population in the NE and as
they are the only Heavy Industry in the area, the Committee recommends the Government to accord
priority to its revival/ restructuring and modernisation of HPC. The Committee also feels that the State
Government of Assam may also contribute their bit to help the company in its efforts to regain its lost
ground. (Para No. 89)
Action Taken
Draft Note containing the proposal for revival of HPC has been circulated to concerned departments
for their comments. Based on the comments of concerned departments, draft CCEA Note is being
modified.
HPC has informed that Assam Government is concerned to the problems of HPC and is extending
possible support time to time. Government of Assam (GoA) has given exemption of VAT on purchase
of bamboo. GoA has further assured to consider exemption of V AT on purchase of coal and sale of paper.
Abolition of Educational Cess on purchase of bamboo is also under consideration. GoA is also considering
signing of Moll for supply of paper for 5 years to Assam State Textbook Board.
Recommendation/observation
However, the Committee also takes into account certain issues brought before it during the oral
evidence which include the need for a transparent and efficient bamboo procurement policy and sales
and marketing methods of its paper to various consumers including institutional buyers like State
Governments. The Committee, in this regard, takes into cognizance the submission of DM that they will
request the State governments to buy paper directly from HPC rather than do so through agents.
(Para 90)
Action Taken
The revised and updated bamboo procurement policy has been uploaded on the website so as to
further ensure transparency in bamboo procurement. The revised and updated CS & Marketing Policy
including Institutional Buyers like State Governments who are directly purchasing paper from HPC has
also been uploaded on the Website.

20
As per the advice of the Committee, HPC shall take up with the State Governments through DM
for issuing GO/Notification (direct purchase of paper from HPC) without any involvement of Agent.
Recommendation/observation
Coming to the issue of procurement of bamboo, the Committee is of the opinion that this should
be made an avenue for the small and marginal bamboo farmers are to sell their produce at the best
remuneration to HPC directly. The Committee is sure that this will also ensure the cheapest priced
bamboo for the Company. In this regard, the Committee draws attention to the stress laid in the current
Budget towards legally streamlining and promoting contract farming to ensure best prices to farmers.
Accordingly, it is recommended, that DHI and HPC shall consider entering into captive farming contracts
with local farmers. Assistance can also be sought from the State Government to fulfil the requirement
of land, if any, in this direction. Further, the Committee is also of the opinion that HPC should keep
in mind a medium to long term goal of migrating to an alternate and more environment-friendly fuel.
(Para 91)
Action Taken
The recommendation of Committee noted. HPC is already having a Gate Purchase Scheme under
which bamboo is purchased directly from farmers without involvement of any Agent. This system will
be further strengthened.
HPC shall also approach State Government for allotment of barren/unutilised land for captive
plantation of bamboo.
The suggestion of Committee to migrate to alternative and more environmental friendly raw material
is noted and possibility of the same shall be explored accordingly.
Recommendation/observation
Still further, the Committee would want DHI to actively pursue the possibility of securing funds for
the revival/restructuring of its CPSEs in NER from the Non-lapsable pool of resources for NER.
(Para 93)
Action Taken
Draft Note containing the proposal for revival of HPC has been circulated to concerned departments
for their comments. Based on the comments of concerned departments, draft CCEA Note is being
modified. Suggestion of the Committee to secure funds for the revival of HPC from the non-lapsable pool
of resources for NER is noted and possibility of the same will be explored.
Recommendation/observation
The Committee finds that revival of NEPA Ltd. was approved by the CCEA in September, 2012 with
a CAPEX of ` 285 crore (out of which ` 157.00 in the form of fresh equity by GoI and balance ` 128
Crore through bank loans) for RMDP. Out of the pledged Government support of ` 157 crore the
Committee has been informed that an amount of ` 104.58 crore provided during 2015-16 is to be utilized
by March, 2017 for RMDP. The Committee's expectation was that this year the remaining Government
support will be provided and NEP A is pursuing, with the help of DHI, avenues for bank loan components.

21
However, the Committee expresses its disappointment that the date of completion of the RMDP has been
extended from March to June, 2017 and no budgetary support is extended for NEP A for this year.
(Para 97)
Action Taken
Government accorded approval to the proposal for revival of NEPA Limited with CAPEX of ` 285
crore. Out of this, GoI equity infusion was ` 157 crore and balance amount of `128 crore to be raised
by the Company from Banks/Financial Institutions. Funds of ` 157 crore have already been released by
GOI in 4 instalments; last one of ` 47.91 crore was released on 31.03.2016. Therefore no budgetary
support is extended for NEPA this year.
As per contract, CPP renovation works were to be completed by June 2017, however the vendor
agreed to squeeze the schedule. Demonetisation has affected the progress of works and vendor could
not manage to squeeze the schedule. Best efforts are being made to complete the project early.
Company is still on old 1997 scales. Salary support since April 2014 is pending for release. Since
February 2016, Company is anyhow managing to release only 50-60% salary and wages advance for
sustenance of employees. This is leading to de-motivation and also affecting the progress.
The original sanctioned RMDP budget was ` 285 crore However, the revised budget estimate of
RMDP now works out to be ` 428 crore due to cost escalations and additional items for the overall plant.
Proposal for Revised Cost Estimate is being included in the CCEA Note for salary support.
The process of balance loan ` 128 crore from the Banks (SBI & BOI) is under consideration. DHI
has given approval of mortgage of Plant and Machinery and immovable property at Delhi. SBI, the lead
bank, sought a revised TEV report. For the purpose, consultant was appointed. Draft TEV report has
already been prepared and sent to SBI and is under review at their end. They have also indicated
requirement of credit rating. Tender for the same has already been floated and the work will be finished
within a month. Loan is likely to be sanctioned in May/June, 2017.
Recommendation/observation
Also, the Committee finds that NEPA has scaled up its tentative production performance to 
` 306
crore for 2017-18 compared to ` 13.75 crore (anticipated) performance during 2016-17. The Committee
appreciates optimism expressed by NEPA and presumes that the Company expects to do well during
2017-18 as RMDP is to be completed during the year. However, if that is the case the Committee finds
it difficult to comprehend why NEP A expects a tentative loss of 
` - 8.60 crore for 2017-18 despite the
projected surge in production performance. The loss figure gets stark when compared to the anticipated
profit of 
` 11 crore for 2016-17. The Committee wants the Department to go into the matter and furnish
an explanation for this ironical situation with regard to the performance of NEP A. (Para 98)
Action Taken
The anticipated profit for the Financial year 2016-17 was ` 11 crore after taking into account profit
of ` 89 crore on transfer of 803 acres Hempur Land to Government of Uttarakhand. Despite best efforts,
transfer could not be finalized during 2016-17. The process is now in final stage and funds are likely
to be received in May 2017. Excluding this exceptional item, anticipated loss for F.Y . 2016-17 is
` 78 crore, which mainly consists of salaries and wages of ` 36.50 crore, VRS of ` 5 crore, interest
of ` 22 crore on GOI loan and establish expenses of ` 11 crore.

22
After implementation of RMDP, NEPA would be able to produce quality paper/newsprint of 100,000
TPA. RMDP completion was targeted in June, 2017 and as such, operations were considered for part
of the year only, with targeted production of 74,250 MT.
During the first year with 9 months operation, company was able to contain the loss to ` 8.60 crore
only, after taking care of interest on GOI loan (salary support) and bank loan and higher depreciation
of RMDP .
Recommendation/Observation
Further, the Committee takes into account the recommendation of the NITI Aayog that the revival
process of NEP A may be permitted to complete and the Company may be reviewed for strategic
disinvestment. Firstly, the Committee disagrees with the dichotomous approach adopted by the NITI
Aayog. It is obvious that the uncertainty regarding the status of the CPSE will dangle above the
Company until a final decision is taken and is certain to affect the morale of the employees. This itself
can impinge the post revival performance of NEPA. At the same time the Committee also feels that,
NEP A can sway the decision on disinvestment, if any, in their favor by coming up with outstanding
performance after revival. The Committee recommends that DHI shall extend all support to NEPA in this
regard. (Para 99)
Action Taken
DHI is taking necessary steps to extend support to NEPA Limited. A proposal for budgetary support
for payment of salary/wages of employees of NEPA Limited is under process. For successful implementation
of RMD, Revised Cost Estimate proposal of NEPA Limited is also under consideration. NEPA will
certainly be motivated to come out with an outstanding performance.
Recommendation/observation
The Committee recommends that the above submissions made by the associations may be appropriately
considered for favourable implementation to the extent possible as creating a facilitating environment
for the private industry to prosper will be decisive in the growth of Capital goods sector in the Country.
The Committee also feels that the Capital Goods Industry should be accorded priority status while
formulating initiatives to improve 'Ease of Doing Business' in the Country. The demands put forth by
the association which does not directly fall under the purview of the Department may be taken up for
inter-ministerial consultation. (Para 102)
Action Taken
The Industry Associations were involved in formulation of the National Capital Goods Policy. The
ongoing Capital Goods Scheme, presently under implementation in the Department of Heavy Industry is
based on the recommendations of the Report of the Working Group on Capital Goods that was constituted
under the aegis of the erstwhile Planning Commission. Industry Associations participate in the Development
Councils for the CG Sub Sectors in a regular manner to air their issues. In other words, DHI actively
involves Industry Associations before planning any policy interventions and take up their issues with
other Ministries like Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Commerce etc. The issues concerning CG Industry,
which include issues raised by the Industry Associations, have been taken up in the Inter Ministerial
Standing Committee for Capital Goods. Meeting and follow up action has been initiated.
Recently Development Council meetings for Machine Tools Industry and Textile Machinery Industry
have been held on 24.05.2017 and 16.05.2017 with active participation of the Industry/Industry Associations.

REPORT
The Industrial sector in India had seen in the recent past many policy interventions by the Government
that include, measures to improve the Ease of Doing Business, Start Up India initiative, Digital India programme,
formulation of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), the introduction of Goods and Services Tax
(GST) and the umbrella promotion of domestic production under the flagship ‘Make in India’ scheme, etc.
There has been invigorated emphasis on infrastructure and tangible inroads have been made in the construction
of highways, railways, power and other infrastructure sectors. Such decisive action has resulted in impetus
to the Heavy Industries sector which broadly encompasses Machines Tools, Heavy Engineering and Electrical,
Industrial and Textile machinery, Earth Moving Equipments & Tractor and Automobile industry.
2. As per the Economic Survey 2017-18, the effect of the efforts of the Government has been reflected
in the fact that the India has leabt 30 ranks over its previous rank of 130 in the World Bank’s latest ‘Doing
Business Report, 2018’. The industry associations like Automotive Component Manufacturers Association
of India (ACMA) and Confederation of Indian Industry (CIl) are also of the opinion that the recent policy
initiatives and infrastructural ventures of the Government along with the allocations made in the Union
Budget, 2018-19 are to become beneficial in the coming days to the various sectors under Heavy Industry.
According to them, policy initiatives like GST, National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), and IBC along
with Non-performing asset (NPA) Ordinance and infrastructure projects like Bharatmala (announced in the
Budget 2018-19) aiming to build highways and roads across the country would have cascading benefits for
various Heavy Industry sub-sectors like earth moving, mining, heavy electric equipment, etc.

Vision and Mission of DHI
5. According to the official website of DHI, the Vision and Mission statements of DHI are as follows:
Vision
To have Modern, Healthy and Robust Auto, Heavy Engineering, Heavy Electrical and Capital
Goods Sectors and Self-reliant and Growth Oriented Public-Sector Undertakings under the
Department.
Mission
/circle6The Department of Heavy Industry strives to bolster profit making PSEs as well as restructure
and revive sick and loss-making PSEs under its administrative control.
/circle6The DHI seeks to achieve its vision of global automotive excellence through creation of state-
of-the-art Research and Testing infrastructure through the National Automotive Testing and R&D
Infrastructure Project (NATRIP).
/circle6The DHI seeks to achieve its vision by providing necessary support to the Auto, Heavy Engineering,
Heavy Electrical and Capital Goods Sector.
6. Regarding the operating CPSEs, under the administrative control of Department of Heavy
Industry, the Committee notices that their number has begun to dwindle since 2016-17. From a
total of 31 in 2016-17, they have come down to 24 in 2017-18 and currently the number of operating
CPSEs under DHI have been reduced to 22. According to the data submitted by DPE before the
Committee, amongst the Ministries/Departments of Government of India it is DHI that has seen
the largest attrition rate of CPSEs - 10 that have been approved for closure and 6 that have been
approved for strategic disinvestment.
7. In this regard, the Committee takes into cognisance the fact that depending on the NITI
Aayog’s classification of ‘High Priority’ areas for Government Ownership, CPSEs which are in
profit or those that can very well be revived/restructured can also be strategically disinvested/
closed, if they do not fall under the priority areas. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that
DHI should start classifying CPSEs under it, in tune with the ‘High Priority’ areas identified for
Government ownership. Such classification would help the Department focus its attention and funds
on CPSEs that would be identified for retention under Government ownership as per extant policy.
In the opinion of the Committee, this would in turn give more meaning to the Department’s Mission
and Vision statements.
8. Also, the Committee is of the opinion that it would be prudent for DHI to study the goods/
services offered by the CPSEs intended/identified for closure or strategic disinvestment and
understand the manner in which the void likely to be created in the market due to the absence of
Government ownership of these CPSEs is going to get filled. If such demands are proposed to be
met by imports, including cheap second-hand machinery/goods, rather than by domestic production,
then it must be assumed that the closure/strategic disinvestment would be antithetical to national
priority of promoting domestic production and ‘Make in India’ initiative and would be a matter of
great worry. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the Department should commission a
research study to find reasons as to why they are losing CPSEs dealing with goods/services under

4
the Heavy Industries Sector. The study should also focus on the market demand currently being
met by these CPSEs and how the said demand would be met in case of their closure/strategic
disinvestment.

11. While examining the Demand for Grants (2018-19) for DHI, the Committee observed that the budgetary
allocation for the Department under the Revenue Expenditure for the last five years has gone up from ` 221
crore (RE) to ` 801 crore (RE) and the Capital Expenditure, during the same period, had gone down from
` 1034 crore (RE) to ` 306 crore (RE). The Committee further observed that the increase in Revenue
Expenditure (which is considered to be non-productive) and decrease in Capital Expenditure (which is
considered to be used for asset cteation) was not a healthy financial trend. In this regard, Secretary, DHI
while agreeing that there is a general perception that Revenue Expenditure is not productive expenditure
stated that the schemes under DHI have both Revenue and Capital Expenditure. Further clarifying this, he
submitted that when a subsidy is given under a scheme, in the long run, it was considered as productive
expenditure because its end result is productive. Because of this, the expenditure on the schemes of
Department of Heavy Industry cannot be classified in the closed compartments of ‘productive’ and
‘unproductive’.

5
12. Further, an analysis of the budget figures of DHI for the last three years shows that there has been
significant fluctuation between the Budget Estimates (BE) and Revised Estimates (RE) figures of the Capital
Expenditure. During 2015-16, the BE under Capital Expenditure of ` 1349 crore went down to ` 664 crore
at RE. In 2016-17, the BE for Capital Expenditure was ` 907 crore and it swelled up to ` 2354 crore at RE.
Again in 2017-18, ` 1615 crore BE went down to ` 306 crore during RE under Capital Expenditure. But the
actual utilisation of the said Revised Estimates under Capital Expenditure during all these years has almost
been complete.
13. In this regard, the Committee would like to suggest that such a wide gap between Revenue
and Capital Expenditure under Revised Estimates (RE) in the Budget allocations of DHI does not
paint an ideal financial picture and needed to be looked at with a holistic/balanced approach. From
the submission of the Department, the Committee infers that huge fluctuation in the Budget
Estimates (BE) and Revised Estimates (RE) in terms of Capital Expenditure figures is broadly due
to delays in approval for the anticipated closure/restructuring packages of CPSEs. Such unforeseen
delays in approval take out large amount of funds at Revised Estimates (RE) stage. This, combined
with the Revised Estimates ceiling prescribed by Ministry of Finance based on pace of expenditure,
which is applicable to the entire Budget allocations, affects the key projects like NA TRiP, FAME-
India, AUSC, etc. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that DHI should initiate appropriate
action and avoid such vast fluctuations between BE and RE allocations in future in consultation with
the Ministry of Finance (MoF).
Automobile Industry of India
14. Automobile Industry was delicensed in July 1991 with the announcement of the New Industrial
Policy, whereas, the passenger car got delicensed only in 1993. The norms for foreign investment and
import of technology have also been progressively liberalized over the years for vehicles manufacturers
to make this sector globally competitive. At present, 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FOI) is permissible
under automatic route in this sector including passenger car segment. The auto-industry is a key employment
generator, in which the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) manufactures the vehicles, the inbound
auto component and logistics industry makes and delivers component and systems and the outbound
logistics and dealer network sells, maintains and distributes the vehicles. Every vehicle produced, generates
secondary and tertiary employment. The industry generates employment of 13 persons for each truck, 6
persons for each car and 4 persons for each three-wheeler and 1 person for two-wheelers. As such the
sector has multiplier effect on economic activity. If the industry produces as per its potential, it could
support employment of over 65 million people by 2026. The Government, recognizing the importance of
the automobile industry in the Indian economy, is currently working with targets set in the Automotive
Mission Plan 2016-26. The DHI is also developing an automotive policy for holistic development of the
sector in India.
15. The Industry produced a total 14.7 million vehicles which included passenger vehicles, commercial
vehicles, three wheelers and two wheelers in April-September, 2017 against 13.4 million in April- September,
2016 (% of growth rate is 9.18%). In April-September 2017, overall automobile exports were 1.95 million,
against the same period i.e. April-September 2016 of 1.76 million (% of growth rate is 10.71%).

(ii) Scheme for Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid and) Electric Vehicle in India —
FAME - India
26. As part of the National Mission on Electric Mobility Plan 2020 (NEMMP), DHI formulated a scheme
namely,. FAME-India, to promote hybrid/electric technology in transportation to reduce dependency on
fossil fuel. The scheme was proposed to be implemented over a period of 6 years, till 2020, wherein it is
intended to support the hybrid/electric vehicles, market development and its manufacturing eco-system to
achieve self-sustenance at the end of the stipulated period. At present, the Phase-I of the scheme is under
implementation, which was originally for a period of 2 years commencing from l “ April 2015 i.e. FY 2015-
16 and FY 2016-17 and has since been extended now till 31st March 2018. As per the original scheme, Mild
hybrid, Strong Hybrid, Plug-in Hybrid and Pure Electric technologies (collectively termed as xEV) were
covered in the Scheme. However, “Mild Hybrid” technology has been excluded from the Scheme w.e.f.
01/04/2017.
