57. During a Committee meeting in year 2021, the Committee was apprised that KVIC 
is assessing the recycling of working capital (working cycle) @ 16 months but on the 
other hand the banks are calculating it at 4 months and this is the bone of contention 
between KVIC and banks and this situation is affecting the ISEC Scheme adversely. The 
Committee desired to know whether any consensus has been reached between KVIC and 
banks for bringing uniformity between the methodology used by KVIC to issue ISEC 
certificate and the working capital calculation methodology adopted by banks for bridging 
the gaps between ISEC being certified by KVIC and working capital amount sanctioned 
by banks, as the issue is a long standing one.   The Ministry informed the Committee that 
the Chief Advisor (Cost), Ministry of Finance, Gov ernment of India conducted a study to 
ascertain an appropriate Working Capital Formula for ISEC Scheme. The study report has 
been placed in a consultation meeting conducted with representatives of major  Khadi 
Institutions/federations and other stakeholders of Khadi  programme. The representatives 
of Khadi institutions/Federations present in the meeting unanimously opposed the 
shortening of the operating cycle for working capital for the Khadi  programme and for 
retaining the existing Working Capital Formula and further suggested for the conduct of a  

23 
 
study considering the peculiarity of working conditions/decentralized nature of activities 
of Khadi sector. Subsequently, the matter was also discussed with the Bankers who were 
of the view that the KVIC‟s ISEC working capital formula should be modified/brought 
down for acceptance of banking norms.  Further, a committee has been constituted to 
study the existing working capital formula. 
 
58. The Committee observes that the actual Interest Subsidy Eligibility 
Certificates issued and funds released by Banks are not very encouraging and 
creates gap in working capital requirement and actual fund availability as a result of 
which the Khadi Institutions fail to achieve the desired level of performance.  It has 
been brought to the notice of the Committee time and again that KVIC and banks 
are adopting a different working capital formula.  KVIC is assessing the recycling of 
working capital (working cycle) @ 16 months but on the other hand the banks are 
calculating it at 4 months and this is the bone of contention between KVIC and 
banks, which appears to be one of the lacuna e for the gap existing between ISEC 
issued and Bank finance .  T he Committee observes that this issue needs to be 
addressed at the appropriate level.  The Committee strongly recommends that a n 
amicable formula may be devised by KVIC and banks, which is acceptable to both 
in order to increase the efficiency and efficacy of the ISEC scheme. 
 
59. The Committee observes that the ISEC issued and bank finance provided to 
the Institutions is yet to reach its full potential . The Committee , therefore, 
recommends that remedial measures should be taken by the Ministry to address the 
issues and create awareness drive through various available modes to popularize the 
Scheme to increase the off take .  The procedures may be simplified, formalities may 
be kept at minimum, and banks may be educated about the Scheme and advised t o 
adopt friendly and favourable approach while considering the applications and 
claims.

90. During the examination of Demands for Grants (2022 -23), the Committee sought a 
response from the Ministry whether the Ministry had carried out any study to assess the 
formal credit availed by MSME Sector and whether there has been a gap between credit 
actually disbursed vis-a-vis the total demand and the steps t aken by the Ministry to bridge 
the gap between the disbursement and credit demand. In response, the Ministry informed 
the Committee that according to the International Finance Corporation (IFC) Report, 
"Financing India‟s MSMEs", November 2018, the addressa ble credit gap for the MSME 
Sector stood at Rs. 25,80,000  crores. Further, based on the said IFC Report, the Expert 
Committee on Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, constituted by the Reserve Bank of 
India in December, 2018, under the chairmanship of Shri  U.K. Sinha also estimated the 

33 
 
overall credit gap in the MSME sector to be in the range of Rs. 20 lakh crore to Rs. 25 
lakh crore. 
 
91. The Ministry further apprised the Committee that various initiatives had been 
undertaken by RBI to increase the credit f low to the Sector, the details of which are as 
follows:- 
 A target of 7.5 percent of Adjusted Net Banking Credit (ANBC) or Credit 
Equivalent Amount of Off Balance Sheet Exposure, whichever is higher, has been 
prescribed for Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs)  for lending to Micro 
Enterprises.  
 SCBs have been mandated not to accept collateral security in the case of loans up to 
Rs. 10 lakh extended to units in the MSE sector. 
 To solve the problem of delayed payment to MSMEs, RBI has come out with the 
guidelines for setting up and operating the Trade Receivables Discounting System 
(TReDS). The scheme is for setting up and operating the institutional mechanism to 
facilitate the financing of trade receivables of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs) from corporate and other buyers, including Government departments and 
Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) through multiple financiers.

Regional Offices of RBI had been advised to organize two/three Town hall meetings in a 
year in MSME clusters, preferably unbanked/underbanked clusters. The objective of the 
Town hall meetings is to create awarene ss of banking facilities among MSEs and linking 
them to the formal banking system. 
 
93. The Committee noticed that overall credit gap in the MSME Sector is in the 
range of Rs. 20 lakh crore to Rs. 25 lakh crore.  The Committee observes that

MSMEs are critical to unlocking the potential of India envisioned under the 
'Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan' campaign and in an endeavour to make India        
$5 trillion economy by 2024 .  The Committee  recommends that remedial steps 
should be taken by the Government to bridge the credit gap of the MSME sector , 
which may prove to be very beneficial for the overall strengthening of MSME Sector 
and also address the problem of credit crunch of MSME Sector. 
 
 

34 
 
94. The Committee observes that a large chunk of Micro enterprises are 
operating in an informal sector and therefore they are not eligible for formal credit 
offered by financial institutions and these Micro enterprises are often deprived of 
benefits announced by the Government under various schemes meant for MSMEs. 
Another reason is lack of awareness among the Micro entrepreneurs because most of 
the times the intended beneficiaries either know very little about the various schemes 
or know nothing to take advantage of it. The Committee recommends that adequate 
remedial steps should be taken by the Government to bring these informal Micro 
enterprises in the formal sector by offering various incentives for t hem and by 
creating adequate awareness among them about various schemes offered by 
Government for their welfare.   
 
 
95. The Committee observes that there is no updated data about MSMEs in the 
country.  Further, t here is lack of  data about manufacturing activities in th e 
country.  In the absence of adequate and granular data, the policies and guidelines 
that the Government frames often misfire.  The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that data should be collected about the MSMEs in  the country and thereafter 
policies and guidelines should be designed for the benefit of MSMEs accordingly. 
 
96. The MSME Sector of India is considered as growth engine of the nation. The 
Committee feels that if nurtured properly, the MSME sector has the potential to 
make India an economic superpower.  Therefore, the Committee recommends that 
proper attention must be paid for the all -round development of MSME Sector and 
Government may try to increase the contribution of MSME s in the National 
economy. 
 
97. The Committee recommends that a countrywide comprehensive study needs 
to be conducted on the adverse impact of Covid pandemic on MSME Sector in order 
to devise action plan and strategy to shield and strengthen the MSME Sector. The 
findings of the report may also be shared with the Committee for perusal. 
 
Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) 
 
98. The Ministry informed the Committee that it is in the process of finali zing a new 
Scheme viz. Raising and Enhancing MSME Performance (RAMP). RAMP is a World 
Bank assisted Central Sector Scheme, supporting various RAMP would be a 
Programme for Results (PforR) and the funds would flow through RAMP into the 

35 
 
Ministry‟s budget against mutually agreed Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs). The 
objectives of the programme are:  
 Strengthening coordination and institutions at the National and State level; 
 Building and integrating technology platforms; 
 Enhancing firm capabilities and access to markets; 
 Strengthening the receivables financing markets; 
 Enhancing guarantee products towards increased greening and gender participation ; 
and 
 Expanding access to Online Dispute Resolution Mechanism (ODR). 
 
99. The total outlay for RAMP is Rs. 6,062.45 crore over the five year period 
2022-23 to 2025 -26.  Out of this, Rs.  3750 crore or USD 500 million would be a 
World Bank loan and USD 308 Million or Rs. 2312.45 crore would be the 
counterpart funding by the Government of India through Budgetary support. 
 
Design of the programme:   
 
 
100. The programme has identified two results areas viz:-  
 
(i) Strengthening Institutions and Governance of the MSME Programme. 
(ii) Support to Market Access, Firm Capabilities and Access to Finance. 
 
RAMP focuses primarily on building capacity of National and  State level agencies, 
building platforms for the provision of critical services to MSMEs and enhancing 
outcomes from competitiveness related schemes. RAMP is designed to support 
selected ongoing M /o MSME support programmes, particularly focusing on the 
competitiveness aspects.  
 
101.      The existing Schemes that are being supported by RAMP are: 
 
 MSME Champions Scheme; 
 Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme; 
 International Co-operation Scheme; 
 Capacity Building for Technology Centres; and  
 Research and Evaluation Studies. 
 
102. The Committee observes that as per the information available, RAMP is a 
multi-faceted initiative of the Government assisted by the World Bank to develop 
capacities of MSMEs with administrative, financial, infrastructural and           
techno-managerial support , which is y et to be launched on the ground. T he 

36 
 
programme is expected to develop and upscale MSMEs at least in the focal States 
and MSME Associations are eagerly wait ing for launching of the programme and 
capture the pay -offs. The Committee notes that a weakness of the programme  may 
prove to be reliance on Government machinery and agencies for implementation of 
planned interventions. These agencies and offices are already implementing the 
respective schemes and notwithsta nding the handholding and capacity building by 
global experts, under the aegis of World Bank, scope for improvements may be 
limited. The Committee recommends that following global practices , MSME 
federations and stakeholders may also be involved in impleme ntation of the 
programme components under guidance and supervision of the Government. Th e 
Committee further recommends that the information about the progress made and 
the modalities of the RAMP Scheme may also be furnished to the Committee for its 
perusal as and when these are available.
